summary: Iteration-3 testing of the two new features (genuine offline Aadhaar Secure QR decode + per-camp versioned Prescription Template Editor) plus regression sanity. Backend: extended the pytest suite with a new file /app/backend/tests/test_iter3.py (23 new cases) on top of the existing 74 -> 97 total, 96 PASS / 1 FAIL. New backend coverage: /api/aadhaar/decode (demo payload with computed age, synthetic genuine Secure QR built as gzip AND raw-zlib of 0xFF-delimited fields -> correct name/gender/dob/last4/address, source=secure_qr, female + year-only DOB fallback, old XML PrintLetterBarcodeData QR, random text -> garbage, long random digits -> garbage, snp: and /p/ -> not-aadhaar); /api/templates (defaults=7 blocks from camp name/venue, admin-only RBAC on GET/draft/publish/active with a cookie-free session, 404 for unknown camp, publish-without-draft 400, draft save + GET persistence + upsert-not-duplicate, logo >2MB rejected, logo image/gif rejected, one-A4-page guard 400 'Template exceeds one A4 page', hidden blocks excluded from the guard, publish versioning v1->v2 + /templates/active reflects newest version, restore-defaults resets to 7 blocks and keeps the published version, no raw _id leak); desk print response now contains prescription.camp_id. Frontend (Playwright 1920x1080 + 390x844 self-register): Template Editor tab loads for the active camp, Restore defaults -> 7 blocks, title/subtitle/footer edits reflect live in the A4 preview, block rename/height/visibility reflect in preview (hidden block disappears), reorder via tpl-block-down/up works, sponsor logo upload adds a row + renders in preview, >2MB file rejected client-side with 'Logo must be 2 MB or smaller.', Save draft shows 'Draft saved.', publish with a 250mm block shows the server one-page guard error, valid publish shows 'Published v2' badge + message. Aadhaar scanner in the Desk New Registration modal and on public /self-register: all three capture modes present; camera actually started in the test browser (fake device) with a working Stop camera button and no crash; photo upload of a QR-less image shows 'No Aadhaar QR found in the image. Try a clearer photo.'; USB/paste -> Demo card -> Decode locks identity ('Identity locked from card (demo)'), makes name/age/last4/address read-only and the gender select disabled; garbage paste shows the amber 'Could not read...' warning; full desk registration end-to-end succeeded and the exact decoded identity persisted (TESTQA Sita Devi / Female / 51 yrs / MG Road Rampur -> row #13); template-driven A4 print (/print/prescription/:id) renders the published custom title, subtitle, footer, renamed block, omits the hidden block, shows the identity block (reg no/name/age/sex/phone/address) + patient QR svg and the sponsor logo ; /self-register mobile flow scan->submit->receipt #14 works; regression mark-seen -> Undo from the desk keeps the Printed badge; all 7 admin tabs render and Camps & Days loads. ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND (HIGH): any Secure QR payload longer than 4300 decimal digits decodes as 'garbage' because int(qr) hits Python 3.11's default sys.int_max_str_digits limit - real Aadhaar Secure QR v2 payloads (with the embedded photo, ~1.5-3 KB compressed) are exactly in that range, so genuine cards will be rejected in production.

critical.issue: GENUINE Secure QR payloads >4300 decimal digits always return outcome=garbage ('Could not decode the Aadhaar Secure QR.'). Root cause: aadhaar._decompress does int(qr) and Python 3.11 raises ValueError 'Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion'; the broad `except Exception` in decode_aadhaar swallows it. Verified: 671 B compressed (1616 digits) -> card OK; 2171 B (5228 digits) -> garbage; 4171 B (10044 digits) -> garbage. Real Secure QR v2 with the embedded JPEG photo is typically 1.5-3 KB compressed, i.e. 3600-7000+ digits, so real cards will fail on-site. Fix: sys.set_int_max_str_digits(<large>) at import (or convert the decimal string to bytes without int()), AND add an explicit payload-length cap + decompressed-size cap (see minor item) since raising the limit re-opens the zlib-bomb path. Regression test added: tests/test_iter3.py::TestAadhaarDecode::test_large_secure_qr_with_photo (currently failing).

minor.issue: Endpoint is unauthenticated (needed by /self-register) with no payload-size limit and no cap on the zlib/gzip decompressed size. Once the int-digit limit above is raised, an attacker can post a small compressed payload that expands to hundreds of MB (decompression bomb). Add max payload length (~16 KB) and use zlib.decompressobj().decompress(data, max_length).

Logo size is validated per-logo on the DECODED bytes (<=2 MB x 6 logos) but the base64 data URL is what gets stored, so a template can legitimately reach ~21 MB and blow Mongo's 16 MB BSON document limit with a raw 500. Verified 6 x 1.9 MB logos (~15.2 MB of base64) were accepted with 200. Also each print/preview then downloads that payload on field tablets. Add a total-template byte cap (e.g. 1 MB of logos) measured on the stored data_url.
All failures are collapsed into `except Exception` with no logging, which is exactly why the 4300-digit failure is invisible. Log the exception (without PHI) so field decode failures are diagnosable.

The one-A4-page guard only sums block['height'] and treats identity/signature blocks as height 0, although they occupy real space on the sheet (~35-45 mm combined). A template with 230 mm of 'lines' blocks plus identity+signature can still overflow to a second page. Consider adding the fixed-block allowance to the sum.

_validate_logos silently truncates to the first 6 logos and silently drops any entry whose data_url does not start with 'data:' - the API returns 200 and the admin never learns their logo was dropped. Return a 400 instead.
Carried over from earlier iterations, still open: CORS_ORIGINS default '*' with allow_credentials=True, and no TTL index on login_attempts.

ui_bugs.issue: Success messages ('Draft saved.', 'Published v2.', 'Restored defaults.') render in the emerald Alert but reuse the warning/alert-triangle icon, so a success reads visually like a warning. Use a check icon for tone=emerald.
The error/success alerts and the 'Published v{n}' badge have no data-testid (had to assert on text). Add tpl-error / tpl-message / tpl-version-badge for reliable automation.

The preview is scaled 0.55 inside a full-height card, leaving a large empty grey area below the sheet (~30% of the panel) on desktop; there is also no live 'this will overflow one A4 page' indicator - the admin only finds out on Publish (server 400).
Carried over: the public page still fires GET /api/auth/me on mount -> 401 in the console on every load (cosmetic).

issues: Test-data noise: 9+ TEST_* camps accumulated from prior iterations, making the camp list and the tpl-camp-select dropdown hard to scan (not a product bug, but consider an admin-side archive/delete of camps)

action_items: CRITICAL: raise/remove the int-string-digit limit in backend/aadhaar.py (sys.set_int_max_str_digits) or decode the decimal payload to bytes without int(), so real Secure QR payloads (>4300 digits) decode; keep the demo path intact. Then re-run tests/test_iter3.py::TestAadhaarDecode::test_large_secure_qr_with_photo.
Add a payload-length cap and a bounded zlib decompression (max_length) to decode_aadhaar; log swallowed decode exceptions.
Cap the total stored template/logo payload (base64 size) so a template can never approach Mongo's 16 MB document limit, and reject (400) instead of silently truncating >6 logos / non-data-url logos.
Include the fixed identity/signature block allowance in the one-A4-page height guard, and show a live overflow warning in the editor before Publish.
Use a check icon for emerald (success) Alerts and add data-testid to the template editor alerts/version badge.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/aadhaar.py::_decompress uses int(qr) - this is the single point of failure for real cards on Python >=3.11 (4300-digit cap). Prefer converting the decimal string to an integer via a chunked/decimal approach or explicitly widen the limit at import time, and unit-test with a >2 KB compressed payload.
decode_aadhaar's blanket `except Exception: return garbage` hides configuration/runtime errors (this bug shipped invisible). Catch specific errors and log the rest.

routes_templates.py stores base64 logo blobs inline in the template document and re-sends them with every /templates/active call; a per-camp asset collection (or GridFS) plus a size budget would keep prescriptions printable on slow camp networks.
The published template is copied (not referenced) on publish, which is correct for versioning; but there is no cap on the number of published versions per camp - consider pruning or capping history.

/api/aadhaar/decode being fully public with unbounded body size is the app's only unauthenticated compute-heavy endpoint - add a body-size limit and simple rate limiting (the login lockout pattern already exists).

rca_of_the_issue: aadhaar._decompress() converts the Secure QR decimal string with int(qr). CPython 3.11 enforces sys.get_int_max_str_digits() == 4300 for int<->str conversions, raising ValueError for longer strings. decode_aadhaar wraps parse_secure_qr in `except Exception` and returns outcome='garbage', so every Secure QR longer than 4300 digits (~1785 bytes compressed - i.e. essentially every real card, which embeds a JPEG photo) is reported to the operator as an unreadable QR. Reproduction: gzip-compress the 0xFF-joined identity fields plus 2000 random bytes (simulating the photo), int.from_bytes -> decimal string (5228 digits), POST /api/aadhaar/decode -> {'outcome':'garbage'}; the same payload with only 500 random bytes (1616 digits) decodes correctly. Mitigation: set sys.set_int_max_str_digits(100000) (or 0) in backend/aadhaar.py at import, or avoid int() entirely, plus cap the input length and the decompressed size.
